stem:
Komal must evaluate the unbracketed expression $9 + 4 \times 3 - 6$. The expression has no exponents.

Which order is correct?

options.text: Multiply $4 \times 3$ first to get $12$, then compute $9 + 12 - 6 = 15$.
Add and subtract left to right first: $(9 + 4) \times 3 - 6$.
The word multiplication is the value of the expression.
The same order also requires evaluating exponents before the terms in this expression.

teacher.key_rationale: Without brackets, evaluate the multiplied term first: 9+12-6=15. Adding first omits term-first order. Treating multiplication as the answer swaps the term label for the value. Requiring exponents extends beyond this expression.
